name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
description: This tagine depends on real preserved lemon and real saffron together - saffron gives the braise its genuine golden color and aroma, which nothing else replicates, and the long, slow braise (traditionally in the cone-lidded clay tagine pot, which channels condensation back down into the dish) is what makes the chicken fall-apart tender, not a quick sauté.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Olives, pickled, canned or bottled, green

ingredients.ingredient: Olives, pickled, canned or bottled, green

steps_detailed: Soak the saffron in a tablespoon of warm water for 10 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the olive oil, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic 4-5 minutes, then add the ginger, cumin, turmeric, and the saffron with its soaking water.
Return the chicken, add the broth, cover, and simmer gently 35-40 minutes until the chicken is fall-apart tender.
Add the olives and lemon juice in the last 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro just before serving.

name: Moroccan Couscous
description: Couscous, tiny steamed semolina granules, is Morocco's most iconic dish, real technique steaming the couscous over the simmering stew itself (traditionally in a two-part couscoussier) so it absorbs the broth's aroma directly, not just soaked in boiling water separately.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, zucchini, chickpeas, cumin, and turmeric in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Pour the boiling broth over the dry couscous, cover, and let steam 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the stew and its broth over the couscous.

name: Moroccan Harira
description: Harira, a tomato-lentil soup with real chickpeas and warming spices, is Morocco's essential Ramadan soup, traditionally thickened at the end with a flour-and-water slurry stirred in while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 5-6 minutes.
Add the lentils, chickpeas, tomatoes, cumin, and turmeric with 2.5 cups water, and simmer 25-28 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Whisk the flour with a little cold water into a smooth slurry, then stir into the soup while whisking constantly, and simmer 3-4 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cilantro before serving.

name: Moroccan Pastilla
description: Pastilla is a real sweet-savory pie, spiced meat wrapped in layered phyllo and dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar on top - this true contrast between the savory filling and sweet, crisp exterior is the entire point of the dish, not an inconsistency to fix.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cinnamon, and ginger in a splash of water 25-28 minutes until tender, then shred and reduce any remaining liquid until nearly dry.
Toast the chopped almonds with the granulated sugar in a dry pan 2-3 minutes.
Layer the phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter, then fill with the shredded chicken and almonds and fold into a sealed package.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 20-22 minutes until deeply golden.
Dust with powdered sugar and a light sprinkle of cinnamon before serving - this sweet finish over savory filling is authentic, not a mistake.

name: Moroccan Msemen
description: Msemen, a square, layered flatbread, gets its real flakiness from a genuine lamination technique - the dough is stretched thin, coated in fat, and folded into a square multiple times before cooking, the same basic principle as puff pastry, and skipping this folding just makes a flat, dense bread instead.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and semolina with warm water into a soft, pliable dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Divide into balls, then stretch each one out very thin on an oiled surface.
Brush generously with melted butter and oil, then fold the corners in to form a square, and fold again into a smaller square - this real lamination is what creates the flaky layers.
Flatten gently and cook in a hot, dry pan, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through in flaky layers.

name: Moroccan Zaalouk
description: Zaalouk, a smoky roasted eggplant and tomato salad, real depth built from genuinely roasting both vegetables until soft, not just simmering them.
steps_detailed: Roast the eggplant at 425F (220C) for 25-30 minutes until completely soft.
Mash the roasted eggplant and simmer with the tomatoes, garlic, cumin, and olive oil 10-12 minutes until well combined and slightly reduced.

name: Moroccan Preserved Lemons
description: Real preserved lemons, salt-cured and fermented over weeks, are the foundation of countless Moroccan dishes - the fermentation itself is what transforms the lemon's bitterness into something deep and savory, and there's no honest shortcut for the real process.

ingredients_full.note: grams, to approximate whole lemons with peel

ingredients.note: grams, to approximate whole lemons with peel

steps_detailed: Quarter the lemons without cutting all the way through, keeping them attached at the base.
Pack the inside generously with salt.
Pack tightly into a sterilized jar, pressing to release juices, cover with the lemon juice, and seal.
Let ferment at room temperature at least 3-4 weeks, shaking occasionally, until the peel is completely soft.

name: Moroccan Ras el Hanout Spice Blend
description: Ras el hanout, meaning 'head of the shop', is real Morocco's most complex spice blend, traditionally containing a dozen or more spices - this simplified version captures the warm, layered character with what's realistically available.
steps_detailed: Toast each ground spice briefly in a dry pan, 30 seconds, just until fragrant - this wakes up their aroma without burning them.
Mix all the spices together thoroughly and store in an airtight container.

name: Moroccan Harissa
description: Harissa, a fiery chili paste, shared across the wider Maghreb, real Moroccan versions often include real caraway alongside the chili.
steps_detailed: Roast the jalapeños directly over a flame or under a broiler until the skins blister, 4-5 minutes, for real depth.
Blend the roasted jalapeño, garlic, cumin, and coriander with the olive oil into a smooth paste.

name: Moroccan Mint Tea
description: Mint tea, sweetened green tea poured with real ceremony from height to build a foam, is absolutely central to Moroccan hospitality - the pouring technique itself is part of the tradition, not just presentation.
steps_detailed: Warm the tea with the mint 5 minutes.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Pour from a height into small glasses to build a light foam on top - a genuine part of how it's traditionally served.

name: Moroccan Beef Tagine with Prunes and Almonds
description: A sweet-savory tagine, real dried fruit and warm spices slow-braised with beef, a classic Moroccan flavor combination, not a modern fusion - real technique toasting the almonds separately so they stay crisp rather than softening in the sauce.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Plums, dried (prunes), stewed, without added sugar

ingredients.ingredient: Plums, dried (prunes), stewed, without added sugar

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the cinnamon, ginger, prunes, honey, and 0.75 cup water, cover, and simmer 35-40 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Toast the almonds in a separate dry pan 2-3 minutes until fragrant, so they stay crisp.
Scatter the toasted almonds over the tagine just before serving.

name: Moroccan Chickpea and Vegetable Tagine
description: A vegetarian tagine built on the same real slow-braise principle as the meat versions, real depth coming from the same warming spice base, finished with fresh herbs for real brightness.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chickpeas, carrot, zucchini, tomatoes, cumin, and turmeric together, covered, 20-22 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes more to reduce the sauce slightly.
Stir in the cilantro just before serving.

description: A simple, fragrant orange and cinnamon salad, a classic Moroccan dessert or palate cleanser after a rich meal.
steps_detailed: Arrange the orange slices on a plate, overlapping slightly.
Dust generously with cinnamon and drizzle with honey.
Scatter the fresh mint over the top just before serving.

description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Morocco.

Toss with a light dusting of cinnamon while still warm, echoing the sweet-spiced almonds used throughout Moroccan cooking.

name: Moroccan Hummus with Argan Oil
description: A simple hummus finished with real argan oil, honoring Morocco's genuine culinary heritage - argan oil is a distinctly Moroccan ingredient, pressed from the kernels of the argan tree native to the country's southwest.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

name: Moroccan Carrot Salad
description: A simple, bright carrot salad with real cumin and lemon, a common Moroccan side, real versions often finished with a scatter of fresh cilantro for genuine freshness.
steps_detailed: Toss the grated carrot with the lemon juice, cumin, and olive oil.
Scatter the cilantro over the top and let sit 10 minutes before serving so the flavors meld.

name: Moroccan Roasted Chickpea Snack
description: A simple roasted chickpea snack, common across Morocco, real technique patting the chickpeas fully dry first so they crisp instead of steam.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Toss the well-dried chickpeas with the oil, cumin, and salt.
Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast at 400F (200C) for 25-30 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Moroccan Beef and Vegetable Couscous
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable couscous, common Moroccan home cooking, real technique steaming the couscous separately over the pot rather than just soaking it, so the grains stay light and separate.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, tomatoes, and cumin with 1.5 cups water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the beef is tender.
Toss the dry couscous with a little oil and water, then steam it over the simmering stew for 10 minutes, fluffing partway through.
Serve the stew over the finished couscous.

name: Moroccan Semolina Cake
description: A syrup-soaked semolina cake, shared across the wider North African and Eastern Mediterranean region, real technique poking small holes across the top before pouring the syrup, so it soaks all the way through rather than pooling on the surface.
steps_detailed: Mix the semolina, sugar, and melted butter into a batter and press into a small baking dish.
Score the top into diamond shapes and press a piece of chopped almond into each.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 20-22 minutes until golden.
While still hot, poke a few small holes across the top and drizzle the honey over so it soaks in fully.
